title: Where to run Smart Compose inference
prompt: Smart Compose predicts the rest of a sentence as the user types, suggesting completions inline. You must decide where the prediction model runs. Pick the deployment approach that fits the constraint.
constraint: Suggestions must keep up with keystrokes (single-digit-to-low-tens-of-ms perceived latency) AND the email content being typed must stay private — sending raw draft text to servers is a privacy concern.

options.why: Each keystroke incurs a network round-trip, so you can't reliably hit keystroke-speed latency, and you must ship the raw, in-progress email content off-device on every stroke — violating both halves of the constraint at once.

Local inference means no per-keystroke network hop, so predictions land within keystroke latency, and the draft text never leaves the device — directly satisfying both the latency and privacy halves of the constraint. The smaller model is the deliberate cost you accept to get there.

Defensible — short, latency-critical completions stay local, preserving the keystroke-speed common path. But the server fallback still sends draft content off-device for longer suggestions, weakening the privacy guarantee, and the routing decision adds latency-sensitive complexity. Acceptable but not the cleanest fit for a hard privacy constraint.

Edge caching can't help: predictions depend on the unique in-progress draft, so there's nothing to cache, and lower network latency still doesn't reach keystroke speed. Worse, the raw email text is still transmitted to servers every keystroke — the privacy concern is untouched.
